claims.statement: OIDC primer link covers concepts/architecture/benefits; link is not full primer review or cloud trust proof.
GHEC data-residency guidance requires substituting certain OIDC values; linked substitutions are separately unresolved, so dotcom issuer values must not be blindly applied.

OIDC requesting job/workflow needs the write access level for the id-token permission to fetch/use a JWT; this scope alone gives no resource modification rights. External short-lived authentication and detailed permission configuration require separate provider trust.

Before OIDC use, plan predictable token allocation and define at least one trust condition blocking untrusted repositories. Conditional Dependabot update tokens carry event_name dynamic; workflow-only trust should allow expected event names where provider supports event conditions. Minimum condition count alone does not prove secure scope.
Multiple on events are alternatives, not conjunctions; push/fork example triggers on either and simultaneous triggering events can produce multiple runs, not automatic deduplication.
Simple on: push example accepts pushes to any repository branch; parent event branch/tag/filter nuances remain separately scoped.

Onboarding links cover templates, CI, packages, deployment, tasks and advanced runners/CLI/concurrency/matrices; certification reference is feature-conditional. Marketing automation breadth is not exhaustive implementation evidence.
Organization access to a larger runner is controlled through its assigned group's organization policy, not a per-runner sharing guarantee or observed permissions.

Organization role permissions separate Actions General policy management excluding self-hosted settings, runner/group management including creation restrictions, secret administration and variable administration. One role does not imply all other administrative rights.

Source says organization Actions write permissions require manually setting enterprise write permissions, with repository/organization links. Parent transfer/inheritance context is unidentified, so this must not become a universal privilege escalation requirement.
Output limit is1MB per job and50MB total per workflow run, approximated using UTF-16 encoding; count is not plain UTF-8 bytes or guarantee of secret output delivery.

Sharing a private action/workflow repository across workflows may expose indirect access through run logs to outside collaborators of consumer repositories despite no direct private-repository access. Sharing access is a confidentiality review decision, not automatic safety.

Public reusable workflows allow SHA/tag/branch refs. For non-SHA refs, rerunning all jobs uses the specified reference, whereas failed/specific-job reruns use the first attempt's commit SHA; reproducibility depends on rerun mode.

Reusable input values passed via job with must match declared boolean/number/string types; named secrets use secrets. Example main ref and PAT secret name are placeholders, not immutable trust or approved credential use.
Same-organization/enterprise reusable calls may use secrets: inherit to pass secrets implicitly. Eligibility is not approval to expose all inherited secrets or proof of downstream safe handling.
Environment configuration requires owner for personal repositories and admin for organization repositories; source requirement is not an actual granted permission or blanket authorization.

Organization secrets/variables creation permits owners and conditionally appropriate custom-role secret/variable managers. Broad prose 'or' is not proof secret-management grants variable-management or vice versa; individual roles remain distinct.
Environment secrets/variables creation requires personal repository owner or organization repository admin; availability and actual authority remain separately observed.

Organization repository secret/variable creation requires write when repo-ci-cd-admin feature applies, otherwise admin; personal repository needs collaborator. Preserve feature branch rather than universalizing write or admin.

Selected actions/workflow policy UI label depends on workflow-policy feature and enterprise versus owner scope; older branch says Allow select actions. Label is not actual policy selection or enforcement proof.

PostgreSQL example client.js uses POSTGRES_HOST/POSTGRES_PORT supplied at Connect to PostgreSQL step. Parent script/service behavior is separately linked, not executed or verified by variable presence.
